publication: The Newark Herald (pp. 1-12) bound with New Jersey Herald News (pp. 13-20)
summary: 20-page scan containing two distinct Newark Black weeklies both dated Saturday, June 11, 1938. Pages 1-12 are The Newark Herald (Vol. 11 No. 18, 'New Jersey's Largest Weekly Newspaper,' published by Newark Herald Publishing Co., Merrill Biddle president, Julius X. Adams managing editor, F. Sweeney Jones business manager), covering the George W. Gregory acquittal, the Dan Winge missing-cashier embezzlement scandal, Braddock training to help Joe Louis, Philip J. Jones named NY Assistant Attorney General, Langston Hughes' mother's death, Society/Society pages, an editorial page, and heavy sports/amusements coverage of Joe Louis, Henry Armstrong, John Henry Lewis, Duke Ellington and Louise Beavers. Pages 13-20 are a separate paper, New Jersey Herald News (Vol. 1 No. 6, 'Owned and Published by New Jersey Negroes,' motto 'Equality Justice Opportunity for the Negro People'), covering Long Branch's race ban at the beach, Jim Crow at the Novelty Bar in Newark, an aged minister attacked by a butcher, Elks state convention planning, and society/sports pages featuring Joe Louis-Schmeling training and Homestead Grays vs Newark Eagles baseball. Both mastheads sharing the same publication date strongly supports the 1942-issue claim that the New Jersey Herald News later absorbed/combined with The Newark Herald.

incidents.what: NJ Supreme Court reverses embezzlement conviction of attorney George W. Gregory, freeing him; expects to resume law practice
Bank/insurance cashier Daniel Winge disappears from Douglass-Harrison Apartments with ~$2,000 shortage, writes letter from Grand Central postmark pledging to tell all

Jim Crow discrimination reported at Novelty Bar & Grill, 220 Market St., Newark; leading Black citizens (Harold Lett, Dr. J. B. Parks, Alma Stemple, Carolyn Hilliard) refused service and grill closed to Black patrons; petition to prosecutor filed
Rev. Charles Thomas, aged minister, attacked and kicked by a butcher at Lincoln Market, 82 South Orange Ave., in a dispute over meat pricing
James Brown, 107, one of last Black GAR Civil War veterans in Chicago, given place of honor in Memorial Day parade
Joe Louis scheduled to fight Max Schmeling rematch at Yankee Stadium; Braddock, Tunney assisting Louis's training at Pompton Lakes camp

connections: The two mastheads (The Newark Herald and New Jersey Herald News) share the identical publication date of June 11, 1938, directly supporting the 1942 New Jersey Herald News masthead's claim of being 'combined with The Newark Herald'
Newark Herald Publishing Co. address (130 W. Kinney St.) matches address used by the 1942-era New Jersey Herald News
Coverage overlaps heavily with NAACP branch activity, Urban League, and NJ Elks/Masonic conventions referenced in the 1942 NJ Herald News issue read in this same batch
Joe Louis/Newark Eagles Negro National League sports coverage recurs across both 1938 and 1942 issues, indicating a consistent community sports-news thread across NJ Black papers
